verdict.rationale: WezTerm is configured with a real language: a `.wezterm.lua` file whose first-party `wezterm.on` API lets user Lua callbacks run when terminal events are emitted, which is scripting beyond static options. Community users confirm the config is "just Lua code". missing for 10: documentation of a plugin loading or distribution mechanism, breadth of the Lua API surface (e.g. available events and objects), independent hands-on evidence of event-driven scripting.

support.subject: As a developer, I can extend the terminal with scripts or plugins in a real language (Lua, Python, kittens) beyond built-in options

citations.quote: `wezterm.on` causes your specified `callback` to be called when `event_name` is emitted.
Create a file named `.wezterm.lua` in your home directory
With Wezterm it's just Lua code, easy to diff and easy to apply.
The Lua configuration is very intuitive as well.
